LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 11.1.1 INTERVIEWS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.1: Listening and Speaking 11.1.1 Interviews
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 11.1.1 Interviews, part of Strand 11 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: when using the digital device for learners with visual difficulties. Why are interviews important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify reasons for sitting an interview,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 11.1.1 Interviews in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. articulate points clearly and confidently during an oral interview,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 11.1.1 Interviews in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. respond confidently to questions during an interview,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 11.1.1 Interviews in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. Seek clarification during an oral presentation,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 11.1.1 Interviews in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. appreciate the importance of interviews in getting school placement and scholarships.  Listen to and review an audio clip on school placement and scholarship interviews. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing materials or type on appropriate adapted digital devices to perform this task.  Discuss reasons for sitting for a placement and scholarship interview. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they share their views.  Search online and watch video clips on school placement and scholarship interview. Adjust light intensity when using the digital device for learners with visual difficulties. Why are interviews important? 105  Role-play the school placement and scholarship interview, record and share them via mobile phones and other social media channels. Create a conducive environment and adequate space for learners with mobility difficulties and ensure safety for all learners as they role-play and assign activities as per each learner’s abilities.  Conduct mock interviews in pairs or small groups,  Collaborate with peers to record the interviews on digital devices  Share the videos with friends and peers on social media platforms, blogs among others.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 11.1.1 Interviews in the Kenya CBC curriculum.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 11.1.1 Interviews together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Communication and collaboration are enhanced as the learner contributes to group decision making while discussing in

groups reasons for sitting for a placement and scholarship interview.

 Digital Literacy is enhanced as the learner uses digital devise to search online and watch video clips on school placement and

scholarship interviews.

Values:
 Responsibility is achieved as the learner role- plays school placement and scholarship interview with peers.

 Respect is enhanced as the learner collaborate with peers to record interviews on digital devices and shares with peers.

106

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Peace Education is developed as the learner works in harmony with peers to conduct mock interviews and role play.

Link to other subjects:

The learner relates the concept of interviews to the learning of conversational skills in Kiswahili.
